newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt arrests 56 Shi'ite for pushing Iran ideas.
newsitem.headline: Egypt arrests 56 Shi'ite for pushing Iran ideas.

text.p: Egyptian authorities said on Monday they had arrested 56 members of a secret Shi'ite organisation allegedly trying to recruit followers to promote Iranian ideas in the country.
The Interior Ministry said in a statement the Egyptian Shi'ite Moslems were arrested in raids on five provinces across Egypt but did not say when the raids took place.

The majority of Egypt's Moslems are Sunni. The Cairo government has regarded Iran with suspicion ever since its 1979 Islamic revolution and has often accused Iran of trying to export its brand of extermist Islam throughout the region.
The ministry said the Shi'ite organisation had recruited people to send to Iran for training.
"The group also tried to infiltrate political parties and take advantage of them to spread Iranian goals and extremist plans," the ministry said.
Eight of the detained Shi'ites had been to Iran and had contacts with Iranian and Arab Shi'ites, the ministry said.
The government does not prevent Egyptians from travelling to Iran, but those who do are questioned by state security officials upon their return.
A Sunni Moslem militant movement in 1992 launched a bloody campaign to overthrow the government and install a strict Islamic state. More than 1,000 people have been killed in clashes.
